lgd_definition: “Working Dog” shall mean any of various breeds of dogs developed or trained to perform useful work to assist humans (i.e. herding animals, pulling wagons or sleds, or guarding property) and excludes hunting dogs.
collar_tag_req: Every dog Owner shall cause a dog tag to be securely affixed on the dog at all times (until the tag needs replaced).
dog_limit: No person shall have, retain, harbor or have possession of more than three (3) dogs within or about any single detached dwelling, or more than two (2) dogs within or about any dwelling unit. This limit shall not apply to a property which is zoned Agricultural or possesses a valid kennel license.
notes: URL: https://www.hamiltontownship.ca/media/5j2o1bho/by-law-2022-43-animal-control-by-law-repeal-2021-04.pdf. Farm-friendly bylaw that explicitly defines 'Working Dog' to include guarding property and herding, and entirely exempts Agriculturally zoned properties from the 3-dog limit. The Township's Noise By-law (2014-36) also explicitly restricts persistent noise to animals 'kept or used for any purpose other than agriculture', effectively exempting farm dogs.

herding_definition: “Herding Dog” means a Dog that has been trained and used to work as part of a farming operation for guarding, control or protection of Livestock;
collar_tag_req: A Person shall register or renew the registration of a Dog or Cat... Subsection 5.1 does not apply to a Cat kept in the Rural Area or to a Herding Dog.
dog_limit: No limit on the number of dogs per residence.
notes: URL: https://www.cityofkingston.ca/media/ttmlly2u/clerks_bylaw_animals.pdf. Highly farm-friendly bylaw. It explicitly defines 'Herding Dog' to uniquely include the guarding and protection of livestock (which directly encompasses LGDs). Herding Dogs are explicitly exempted from the dog licensing and registration requirements entirely. The City's Noise Bylaw (2004-52) also restricts persistent barking by animals 'kept as household pets', which working farm dogs are not.

collar_tag_req: All dogs living in the Town of LaSalle are required to be licensed and wear a licence in the form of a dog tag.
dog_limit: No Person or household shall own in excess of three Dogs at any one time (exemptions apply for temporary fostering).
notes: URL: https://www.lasalle.ca/media/xtnfxaes/bylaw-8705-animal-control-accessible.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw. A limit of 3 dogs applies, and there are no specific exemptions listed for agricultural properties or farm dogs. The Noise By-law (8706) regulates noise without any explicit exemption for agricultural animals barking.

collar_tag_req: Every Keeper shall ensure that the Tag corresponding to the Licence issued for their Dog is attached to the Dog at all times (except when on the premises of its keeper).
dog_limit: No person shall keep in or about any Dwelling Unit or Premises more than three (3) Dogs. A Premises owner may be exempt from this limit if the Dog is on Premises designated as Agricultural in the Zoning By-law that are more than 0.5 hectares in size and the Dog is sufficiently trained so as to remain on the Premises.
notes: URL: https://www.lakeshore.ca/media/0h2gziai/by-law-27-2023-being-a-by-law-respecting-animal-care-and-control-in-the-municipality-of-lakeshore.pdf. The bylaw is highly farm-friendly because it explicitly exempts properties designated as Agricultural that are more than 0.5 hectares from the 3-dog limit, provided the dog is trained to remain on the premises. Noise By-law 16-2024 also exempts normal farm practices.

collar_tag_req: The municipality does not sell or issue dog tags.
dog_limit: No person may keep upon or in any lands or premises within the Municipality of Lambton Shores more than two (2) dogs, unless a kennel license has been obtained.
notes: URL: https://www.lambtonshores.ca/media/5xknjfjh/by-law-37-2009-control-of-dogs.pdf. The municipality discontinued its dog licensing program so no tags are required or issued. The bylaw strictly limits premises to 2 dogs unless licensed as a kennel, with no specific agricultural exemptions found. Barking is governed by Noise By-law 30-2002, which explicitly exempts normal farm practices under the Farming and Food Production Protection Act.

collar_tag_req: All dogs and cats must be registered, wear an identification tag issued by the City, and be vaccinated against rabies.
dog_limit: The number of mature dogs (16 weeks and older) and cats (over 3 months old) that can be kept in each home is four in total, with a strict maximum of two (2) dogs per home.
notes: URL: https://www.markham.ca/sites/default/files/permits-licenses-taxes/bylaws-off-leash-areas/Attachment%20H%20-%20Animal%20Protection%20and%20Servcies%20By%20law%202018-91.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw for a highly urbanized municipality. Defines 'Law Enforcement Working Dog' but has no provisions for farm dogs or LGDs. Noise By-law 2017-74 regulates excessive noise from animals, such as barking, calling or whining, and does not provide an agricultural exemption.

collar_tag_req: Every Owner of a Dog or Cat shall obtain a new Licence... Pet licenses must be visible on the pet's collar.
dog_limit: The By-law limits the keeping of animals to four (4) per household.
notes: URL: https://www.mississauga.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/21145710/Animal-Care-and-Control-By-law-0098-2004.pdf. Standard urban-focused animal control bylaw. The bylaw features a general pet limit and mandatory registration with no specific exemptions for agricultural operations or farm dogs. The city's noise regulations also restrict barking without agricultural exemptions.

collar_tag_req: Every Owner of a Cat or Dog over the age of twelve (12) weeks shall Licence the Domestic Animal with the Town and shall maintain the Licence in good standing. Licence means an identification tag which is to be affixed to the collar.
dog_limit: No Person shall Keep, possess, or harbour, or permit to be kept, possessed, or harboured more than three (3) Dogs or four (4) Cats within or about any Dwelling Unit, unless the additional Dog(s) or Cat(s) is accompanied by an Owner who does not reside at the Dwelling Unit.
notes: URL: https://www.newmarket.ca/LivingHere/Documents/2020-30%20Animal%20Control%20By-law.pdf. An urban animal control bylaw that caps dogs at 3 per dwelling unit. There are no provisions, definitions, or exemptions recognizing farm dogs, herding dogs, or livestock guardian dogs. The bylaw also strictly prohibits repetitive or persistent barking.

collar_tag_req: Every owner must register the dog and securely affix the dog identification tag to the dog's collar at all times.
dog_limit: Keeping more than three (3) dogs over ten (10) weeks of age on a premises is prohibited unless operating a licensed Hobby Kennel or Breeding Kennel.
notes: URL: https://niagarafalls.ca/media/n0yprszz/animal-control-bylaw-2019-35_03192019.pdf. While the animal control bylaw does not explicitly define working dogs, the City's fine schedule and noise enforcement regulations explicitly exempt 'any domestic pet or other animal kept or used for any purpose other than agriculture' from barking/noise restrictions, rendering it farm-friendly.

collar_tag_req: Every Owner of a Dog, before the 15th day of February in each year... shall licence and register such Dog with the Township.
dog_limit: No person, being an Owner, tenant or occupant of a Property, shall keep, own or Harbour, or permit to be kept, owned or harboured, more than three (3) Dogs per Dwelling Unit (unless holding a valid kennel licence).
notes: URL: https://www.northdumfries.ca/media/phsevkdh/by-law-no-3160-20-regulate-dogs-and-licence-dog-kennels-repeal-by-laws-1268-90-1294-91-2255-07.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw with a 3-dog limit. No explicit provisions or definitions for LGDs or working farm dogs. However, the Township's Noise By-Law (3421-23) explicitly exempts 'normal farming operations' as governed by the Farming and Food Production Protection Act from noise restrictions.
